## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}

content.text:
playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D roguelike inspired by The Binding of Isaac in the existing project.

## Requirements
- Build now without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Create an original, Isaac-inspired game titled “The Binding of Isaac 3D — The Cellar Below,” with three floors, twin-stick-style controls, combat, pickups, bosses, and responsive touch controls.
- Use Three.js via locally vendored modules and procedural assets/audio.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial HTML structure, responsive styling, procedural audio engine, 3D model helpers, dungeon generation, theme definitions, and procedural texture helpers.

### Active
- Finish the playable game implementation; core game loop, renderer/scene setup, controls, combat, room transitions, HUD wiring, and game states remain to be implemented.
- Run the game, debug it, and perform the requested screenshot check.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the existing files and implement the missing game entry point, especially `src/main.js`.
2. Connect dungeon generation, models, audio, HUD, controls, combat, pickups, and floor progression into a complete playable loop.
3. Start the project, test gameplay in a browser, fix issues, and capture/inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.
4. Summarize the finished game and note assumptions briefly.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI markup and module entry point references `./src/main.js`.
- `style.css`: Game presentation, overlays, HUD, and responsive/touch styling.
- `src/audio.js`: Synthesized sound effects and ambient audio.
- `src/models.js`: Three.js procedural player, enemy, pickup, prop, and effect models.
- `src/dungeon.js`: Room generation, floor themes, and dungeon map data.
- `src/textures.js`: Procedural textures and texture helpers.
- `vendor/three.module.min.js`: Vendored Three.js module.
- `vendor/three.core.min.js`: Vendored Three.js core dependency.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `src/main.js` has not yet been created, despite being referenced by `index.html`; the current project is not yet runnable as a game.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D roguelike inspired by The Binding of Isaac in the existing project.

## Requirements
- Build without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at completion.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Create an original Isaac-inspired game titled “The Binding of Isaac 3D — The Cellar Below,” with three floors, twin-stick-style controls, combat, pickups, bosses, and responsive touch controls.
- Use Three.js via locally vendored modules and procedural assets/audio.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial HTML structure, responsive styling, procedural audio engine, 3D model helpers, dungeon generation, theme definitions, and procedural texture helpers.
- Inspected the project files and confirmed `index.html` references a missing `src/main.js`.

### Active
- Implement the missing game entry point: scene setup, game loop, controls, combat, room transitions, HUD, and game states.
- Run and debug the game, then capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `src/main.js` and connect dungeon generation, models, audio, HUD, controls, combat, pickups, and floor progression into a playable game.
2. Start the project and test gameplay in a browser; fix any issues.
3. Save and inspect a small JPEG screenshot, then summarize the finished game and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: UI structure and module entry point referencing `./src/main.js`.
- `src/dungeon.js`: Room and floor generation.
- `src/models.js`: Procedural player, enemy, pickup, prop, and effect models.
- `src/audio.js`: Synthesized sound effects and ambient audio.
- `src/textures.js`: Procedural texture helpers.
- `style.css`: Game presentation, overlays, HUD, and responsive/touch styling.
- `vendor/three.module.min.js`: Vendored Three.js module.
- `vendor/three.core.min.js`: Vendored Three.js core dependency.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `src/main.js` does not yet exist; the game is not yet runnable.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
24: - Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Complete the existing project as a playable 3D roguelike inspired by The Binding of Isaac, then test browser gameplay and capture and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and briefly note them at completion.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px wide) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Build an original Isaac-inspired game titled “The Binding of Isaac 3D — The Cellar Below,” with three floors, twin-stick controls, combat, pickups, bosses, and responsive touch controls.
- Use locally vendored Three.js modules, procedural assets, and synthesized audio.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial HTML structure, responsive styling, procedural audio, model helpers, dungeon generation, theme definitions, and procedural texture helpers.
- Added Three.js renderer and scene setup, base game state, resize handling, room-shell generation, lights, and procedural room clutter.
- Added partial HUD/minimap, floor and room setup, enemy spawning, item definitions, room-clear handling, and enemy damage in `src/main.js`.

### Active
- Finish gameplay in `src/main.js`: input, movement, aiming, shooting, combat updates, pickups, room transitions, bombs, game states, and animation loop.
- Run and debug the game in a browser; capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing `src/main.js` gameplay, input handlers, and initialization.
2. Initialize `models.tex.glowPurple` with a glow texture before calling `Models.createTrapdoor()`.
3. Run the project and resolve runtime or rendering issues.
4. Capture and inspect a small JPEG screenshot, then summarize the finished game and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Scene setup and partial gameplay implementation; remaining gameplay and initialization are unfinished.
- `index.html`: UI structure and module entry point.
- `style.css`: Game presentation, overlays, HUD, and responsive/touch styling.
- `src/dungeon.js`: Room and floor generation; exports `Dungeon`, `DIRS`, and `THEMES`.
- `src/models.js`: Procedural player, enemy, pickup, prop, and effect models; `createTrapdoor()` uses `this.tex.glowPurple`.
- `src/audio.js`: Synthesized sound effects and ambient audio.
- `src/textures.js`: Procedural texture helpers.
- `start.sh`: Project startup entry point.
- `capture.sh`: Project screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `src/main.js` currently imports `makeSoftShadowTexture` but does not use it; `Models` creates its own shadow texture in its constructor.
- `models.tex.glowPurple` is currently unset (`null`); trapdoor creation depends on a valid glow texture.

## Objective
- Complete the existing project as a playable 3D roguelike inspired by The Binding of Isaac, then test browser gameplay and capture and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save visual-check screenshots as JPEGs at ≤1280px wide and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Build an original Isaac-inspired game, “The Binding of Isaac 3D — The Cellar Below,” with three floors, twin-stick controls, combat, pickups, bosses, and responsive touch controls.
- Use locally vendored Three.js modules, procedural assets, and synthesized audio.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added initial UI, styling, procedural audio and assets, dungeon generation, room and floor setup, HUD, enemy spawning, item definitions, and room-clear handling.
- Initialized `models.tex.glowPurple` in `src/main.js` for trapdoor visuals.
- Inspected partial `src/main.js`, dungeon/model/audio code, and UI structure to establish the remaining implementation work.

### Active
- Finish gameplay in `src/main.js`: input, movement, aiming, shooting, combat updates, pickups, room transitions, bombs, game states, and animation loop.
- Run and debug the game in a browser; capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue implementing gameplay, input handlers, and initialization in `src/main.js`.
2. Run the project and resolve runtime or rendering issues.
3. Capture and inspect a small JPEG screenshot, then summarize the finished game and assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Partial scene setup and gameplay; ends at `damageEnemy`.
- `src/dungeon.js`: Room and floor generation.
- `src/models.js`: Procedural models; `createTrapdoor()` uses `this.tex.glowPurple`.
- `index.html`: UI structure and module entry point.
- `style.css`: Game presentation, overlays, HUD, and responsive/touch styling.
- `src/audio.js`: Synthesized sound effects and ambient audio.
- `src/textures.js`: Procedural texture helpers.
- `start.sh`: Project startup entry point.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `src/main.js` imports `makeFloorTexture` and `makeWallTexture` from `src/textures.js`; it also imports `makeGlowTexture` and `makeSoftShadowTexture`, though the latter is unused there. `Models` creates its own shadow texture.
- `src/main.js` currently initializes `models.tex.glowPurple` and defines room rendering, HUD, map drawing, spawning, run startup, room clearing, and enemy damage; gameplay update and input/animation code remain unfinished.

## Objective
- Complete the existing project as a playable 3D roguelike inspired by The Binding of Isaac.
- Test browser gameplay and capture and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save visual-check screenshots as JPEGs at ≤1280px wide and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Build an original Isaac-inspired game, “The Binding of Isaac 3D — The Cellar Below,” with three floors, twin-stick controls, combat, pickups, bosses, and responsive touch controls.
- Use locally vendored Three.js modules, procedural assets, and synthesized audio.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented core gameplay and input handling in `src/main.js`.
- Added procedural glow textures, including `models.tex.glowPurple` for trapdoors.
- Fixed a duplicate `resize()` declaration that caused a syntax error.
- `node --check` passes for `src/main.js`, `src/models.js`, and `src/dungeon.js`.

### Active
- Run the project and resolve any runtime, rendering, or gameplay issues.
- Test browser gameplay, including combat and progression.
- Capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Start the project and inspect browser console/runtime behavior.
2. Test gameplay, combat, and floor progression; fix any issues found.
3. Capture a JPEG at ≤1280px wide and inspect only the latest screenshot.
4. Summarize the result and briefly note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Scene setup and gameplay implementation.
- `src/dungeon.js`: Room and floor generation, doors, themes, and map data.
- `src/models.js`: Player, enemy, tear, pickup, bomb, and trapdoor model factories.
- `index.html`: UI structure and module entry point.
- `style.css`: Game presentation, overlays, HUD, and responsive/touch styling.
- `src/audio.js`: Synthesized sound effects and ambient audio.
- `start.sh`: Project startup entry point.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files appear as untracked in `git status`.
- Syntax checks passed after the `resize()` fix; browser/runtime testing has not yet been performed.

## Objective
- Complete the existing project as a playable 3D roguelike inspired by The Binding of Isaac.
- Test browser gameplay and capture and inspect a small JPEG screenshot.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save visual-check screenshots as JPEGs at ≤1280px wide and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Build an original Isaac-inspired game, “The Binding of Isaac 3D — The Cellar Below,” with three floors, twin-stick controls, combat, pickups, bosses, and responsive touch controls.
- Use locally vendored Three.js modules, procedural assets, and synthesized audio.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented core gameplay and input handling in `src/main.js`.
- Added procedural glow textures, including `models.tex.glowPurple` for trapdoors.
- Removed a duplicate `resize()` declaration that caused a syntax error.

### Active
- Start the project and resolve runtime, rendering, or gameplay issues.
- Test browser gameplay, combat, and floor progression.
- Capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot at ≤1280px wide.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Run syntax checks and start the project.
2. Test gameplay in the browser, including combat and progression; fix any issues found.
3. Capture a JPEG at ≤1280px wide and inspect only the latest screenshot.
4. Summarize results and briefly note assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Scene setup and gameplay implementation.
- `src/dungeon.js`: Room and floor generation, doors, themes, and map data.
- `src/models.js`: Player, enemy, tear, pickup, bomb, and trapdoor model factories.
- `index.html`: UI structure and module entry point.
- `style.css`: Game presentation, overlays, HUD, and responsive/touch styling.
- `src/audio.js`: Synthesized sound effects and ambient audio.
- `start.sh`: Project startup entry point.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- `src/main.js` imports `THREE`, `Models`, `Dungeon`, `DIRS`, `THEMES`, `AudioEngine`, `rng`, `makeFloorTexture`, `makeWallTexture`, `makeGlowTexture`, and `makeSoftShadowTexture`.
- Earlier claimed syntax checks passed, but the latest recorded `node --check src/main.js` failed with `SyntaxError: Identifier 'resize' has already been declared`; the duplicate was then removed, and checks were not rerun afterward.
- Project files are uncommitted and appear untracked in `git status`.

## Objective
- Complete and validate the existing project as a playable 3D roguelike inspired by The Binding of Isaac.
- Test gameplay in a browser and keep the latest visual-check screenshot as a small JPEG.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save visual-check screenshots as JPEGs at ≤1280px wide and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Build an original Isaac-inspired game, “The Binding of Isaac 3D — The Cellar Below,” with three floors, twin-stick controls, combat, pickups, bosses, and responsive touch controls.
- Use locally vendored Three.js modules, procedural assets, and synthesized audio.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented core gameplay, controls, procedural assets, and audio; fixed the duplicate `resize()` declaration, doorway movement bounds, and transition alignment.
- Verified Chromium startup, pause/resume, movement, and a doorway transition into a normal room; no browser console or page errors were observed.
- Combat was attempted in an enemy room; player health decreased, but clearing the room and collecting pickups remain unverified.
- Captured and inspected `screenshots/latest.jpg` at 1024×640; it remains a JPEG at the required size.

### Active
- Continue testing combat outcomes, pickups, bosses, and all three floor transitions; fix issues uncovered.
- Remove temporary `window.__debugState` instrumentation added to `src/main.js` after debugging.

### Blocked
- Combat progression is inconclusive: an enemy room remained “DOORS SEALED” after firing, and the player took damage; no browser errors were observed.

## Next Move
1. Remove the temporary `window.__debugState` global from `src/main.js`.
2. Continue browser testing through enemy-room clears, pickups, bosses, and floor transitions; diagnose and fix any issues.
3. Run final syntax/browser checks and recapture/inspect `screenshots/latest.jpg` if visual changes are made.
4. Summarize validation and briefly state assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Gameplay loop, controls, combat, pickups, and room/floor transitions; currently contains temporary debug instrumentation.
- `src/dungeon.js`: Room/floor generation, doors, themes, and map data.
- `src/models.js`: Procedural player, enemy, projectile, pickup, bomb, and trapdoor models.
- `index.html`: UI structure and module entry point.
- `style.css`: Game presentation, overlays, HUD, and responsive/touch styling.
- `src/audio.js`: Synthesized sound effects and ambient audio.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Latest saved visual-check screenshot.
- `start.sh`: Project startup entry point.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot capture entry point.

## Important Context
- Browser testing used `http://localhost:3000`.
- Movement works; the entrance has generated doors, and holding `KeyW` eventually transitioned into a normal room.
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were reported as untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete and validate the existing project as a playable 3D roguelike inspired by The Binding of Isaac.
- Test gameplay in a browser and keep the latest visual-check screenshot as a small JPEG.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without clarifying questions and briefly note them at completion.
- Save visual-check screenshots as JPEGs at ≤1280px wide and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Build an original Isaac-inspired game, “The Binding of Isaac 3D — The Cellar Below,” with three floors, twin-stick controls, combat, pickups, bosses, and responsive touch controls.
- Use locally vendored Three.js modules, procedural assets, and synthesized audio.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented core gameplay, controls, procedural assets, and audio; fixed the duplicate `resize()` declaration, doorway movement bounds, and transition alignment.
- Previously verified Chromium startup, pause/resume, movement, and a doorway transition into a normal room.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg` was previously captured and inspected at 1024×640; JPEG meets the size requirement.

### Active
- Diagnose why browser automation became extremely slow or timed out; Chromium’s GPU process was consuming ~246% CPU, and subsequent Playwright calls timed out.
- Continue validating room clears, pickups, bosses, and all three floor transitions when browser testing is reliable.
- Remove temporary `window.__debugState` instrumentation from `src/main.js`.
- Run final syntax/browser checks and recapture/inspect `screenshots/latest.jpg` if visual changes are made.

### Blocked
- Combat progression is unverified: the earlier test reported zero enemies while the room remained uncleared; a later run’s output was inconsistent (still in the start room), and later browser tests timed out.
- Pickups, bosses, and floor transitions remain unverified.

## Next Move
1. Investigate browser/GPU test instability and restore reliable Playwright testing.
2. Remove `window.__debugState` instrumentation from `src/main.js` after debugging.
3. Validate room-clearing and continue testing pickups, bosses, and three-floor progression.
4. Run final checks and update the required screenshot only if visual changes are made.
5. Summarize validation and briefly state assumptions.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Gameplay loop, controls, combat, pickups, bosses, floor transitions; currently contains temporary debug instrumentation.
- `src/dungeon.js`: Room/floor generation, doors, themes, and map data.
- `src/models.js`: Procedural player, enemy, projectile, pickup, bomb, and trapdoor models.
- `index.html`: UI structure and module entry point.
- `style.css`: Game presentation, overlays, HUD, and responsive/touch styling.
- `src/audio.js`: Synthesized sound effects and ambient audio.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Latest saved visual-check screenshot.

## Important Context
- Browser testing used `http://localhost:3000`.
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were reported as untracked.
